approvedReference.design: Rounded main glove body dominates the silhouette. Thumb is a compact curved side pad tucked closely against the body, not a second large bulb. White cuff remains distinct. Compare both upright and horizontal reference poses; pose affects apparent proportions.

findings.detail: Large forward-projecting thumb forms a second rounded mass beside the face and broadens the lower silhouette.
Thumb is disproportionately prominent beside the main glove, even allowing for the horizontal supported pose.
Thumb is still too broad and bulbous, though overlap and smaller display size reduce its prominence.
Large low forward thumb competes with the face-bearing main glove body. One of the clearest examples of silhouette drift.
Thumb is closer to a tucked side pad but remains more swollen and prominent than the approved upright reference.

recommendedCorrection: Use the approved Book One glove as the primary anatomy reference for all five images. Reduce and tuck the thumb against the main body, preserving a single dominant rounded glove silhouette. Retain face, expression, glove orientation, scuffed leather, injured white cuff, cushion/support, other characters and scene composition. Preserve original versions and review each edited sibling before substitution. Do not use Book Two or current Book Three Fist anatomy as the primary shape reference.
limits: Qualitative visual review. Image-generation edits can change pixels outside the requested thumb area; no pixel-exact preservation claim. Manuscript prose and Book One remain unchanged.
continuityNote: Historical review of the earlier design. For current Book Three art use the author-approved Fist character sheet, sculpted face, single swept-back thumb fold and red cuff with inset black-outlined white panel.
